sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a complete right femur measuring 180 centimeters in length.
Based on comparisons with other Asian sauropods, this dinosaur was estimated to be approximately 30 meters long, making it one of the longest known dinosaurs.

Fushanosaurus is a sauropod dinosaur genus named after the Fushan Museum in China where its fossils are stored. The only known species is Fushanosaurus qitaiensis, and the entire genus is known only from a single fossil labeled FH000101.
Fushanosaurus belongs to the dinosaur class Saurischia and is classified within the parent group Titanosauriformes.
Although originally classified as a titanosauriform, Fushanosaurus may actually belong to the mamenchisaurid group.
Fushanosaurus lived during the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
